chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskan, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot to perform the first prayer until he had performed the 'Asr prayer. He said: Let him treat the prayer he performed as the first one, then let him begin the 'Asr prayer anew.

He said: I said: What if he forgot both the first prayer and the 'Asr prayer together, then remembered that at sunset? He said: If he is still within a time in which he does not fear missing either of them, then let him perform Zuhr and then perform 'Asr. But if he fears that it will pass him by, then let him begin with 'Asr and not delay it so that it passes him by and both would then have been missed together. Rather, he should perform 'Asr within what remains of its time, then perform the first prayer immediately after it.

key_terms.الْأُولَى: the first prayer, referring here to Zuhr
key_terms.عَلَى أَثَرِهَا: immediately after it, in direct sequence
key_terms.غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِ: sunset, the end of the daytime prayer period
key_terms.فَوْتَ: the passing or missing of the prayer time
key_terms.وَقْتٍ: the remaining legal time for prayer

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if they forgot Zuhr and remembered during the time of 'Asr or near sunset?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding one who forgets Zuhr and remembers after or near the time of 'Asr. It explains how to reorder the prayers depending on whether enough time remains to perform both without missing one. Its significance lies in clarifying the precedence of obligatory prayers and how to act when time is constrained.
